response.title: which power station runs an insulin fridge or medicine fridge the longest
response.answer:
For running an insulin fridge or medicine fridge during a power outage, the power station that lasts the longest depends on two things: its battery capacity (Wh) and how much electricity the refrigerator consumes.

My recommendation is a large LiFePO4 power station with at least 2,000 Wh of capacity, preferably one that supports expansion batteries. For a small, efficient medicine fridge, this could provide several days of backup power.

The important distinction is whether you're powering a tiny portable insulin cooler, a dedicated medicine refrigerator, or a regular household refrigerator. Their electricity requirements can differ dramatically.

Power stations with the longest potential runtime

Here are three high-capacity options. The estimates assume a medicine fridge consuming 300 Wh per day, with 85% usable battery energy. Actual runtime may be shorter because of inverter standby consumption.

Shop

EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X

Longest base runtime here

12,288 Wh capacity

~35 days estimated

Expandable system; very large and expensive

EcoFlow Delta Pro Ultra 6kWh Power Station

6,144 Wh capacity

~17 days estimated

Shop

Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus

5,040 Wh capacity

~14 days estimated

Expandable to 60 kWh

These are illustrative calculations, not manufacturer-guaranteed medicine-fridge runtimes. A smaller DC-powered fridge paired with a smaller power station may be more efficient and economical.

## Calculate runtime for your refrigerator

{@body const [capacity,setCapacity] = DIL.useState("2048")}
{@body const [daily,setDaily] = DIL.useState(300)}

      **{daily} Wh**
    </row>

      <caption>100 Wh</caption>
      <caption>1,200 Wh</caption>

    <caption>Assumes 85% usable energy; excludes additional standby losses</caption>
  </box>
</box>
